writeup.headline: AbCellera rates Sell: a strong share-price run and net cash cannot offset deep losses and a very high valuation.
writeup.thesis: AbCellera scores 39, a Sell, because weak quality and valuation scores outweigh its strong trend and balance sheet. Quality scores 9, with an operating margin of -340.2%, a normalised FCF margin of -458.6% and stock-based compensation at 77.2% of revenue. Valuation scores 0: P/S of 63.2x is high in absolute terms, the FCF yield is 12.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and P/S is more expensive than at 56 of the last 57 month-ends. Growth scores 30 because TTM revenue growth of 101.3% hides a latest-quarter revenue decline of 76.3% year on year, with growth slowed by 172.6 pp from the previous quarter. On the positive side, trend scores 95 with the price 101.5% above its 200-day average and only 8.0% below its 52-week high, and the balance sheet scores 91 with no debt and 4.5 years of cash at the current burn.
key_risks: Revenue is lumpy and fell sharply in the latest quarter, a decline of 76.3% year on year.
Heavy cash burn and stock-based compensation at 77.2% of revenue, with diluted share count up 2.4% year on year.
A P/S of 63.2x leaves little room for disappointment if the Q3 report on November 9 falls short.
After shares rose 156.8% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, a momentum reversal could hit the price hard.
Pipeline value such as ABCL635 depends on clinical results that have not yet produced revenue.
what_would_change: A 6-point rise in the score would lift the rating to Hold. Steadier quarterly revenue that improves the growth score, or a narrower operating loss that improves quality, could do it.
A share-price pullback that lowers P/S from 63.2x could lift the valuation score from 0.
A 10-point drop would mean Strong Sell. A break in the strong trend score of 95, or weak Q3 results or guidance, could cause that.
Clear progress toward positive free cash flow would help both quality and valuation.
